change.author: CarinaWolli

findings.title: Slots inside a date override skip the busy-time check, so double bookings become possible
findings.body: When a slot falls on a date-override day and inside the override window, `dateOverrideExist` is true and the function returns `true` at line 134. It never reaches `busy.every(...)` at line 153. Existing bookings and calendar events on any day that has a date override stop blocking slots, so invitees can book over a meeting the host already has. Instead of returning `true` here, fall through to the busy check (skip only the working-hours check).

findings.title: Working-hours check rejects a slot that falls outside any one range for that day, not outside all of them
findings.body: `workingHours.find` returns true (slot rejected) as soon as one entry for the slot's weekday doesn't contain it. `getWorkingHours` (packages/lib/availability.ts:76-121) often emits several entries per weekday: one per availability range (e.g. 9-12 and 13-17), plus overflow entries when the organizer's local hours cross UTC midnight (lines 103-121). Any slot in one range lies outside the other, so every slot that day is removed. A UTC-8 organizer working 9-17 loses the 00:00-01:00 UTC part, and a split schedule loses every slot. The check should reject a slot only when no entry for that day contains it, i.e. `!workingHours.some(wh => wh.days.includes(day) && start >= wh.startTime && end <= wh.endTime)`.

findings.title: `end` is computed from the slot start, so slots running past the end of working hours are kept
findings.body: `end` uses `slotStartTime.hour()/minute()`, the same value as `start`. `end > workingHour.endTime` therefore never catches a slot that starts inside working hours but ends after them. Use `slotEndTime` here. A slot ending exactly at 00:00 also needs handling, since its minute value wraps to 0.

findings.title: With multiple overrides on the same date, slots in all but one of them are rejected
findings.body: `dateOverrides.find` returns true (slot rejected) when an override on the slot's date doesn't contain the slot. With two overrides on one day (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-17:00), a 15:00 slot lies outside the first one, so it is dropped even though the second override allows it. The slot should be rejected only when it fits none of the matching overrides.

findings.title: Override day is matched on the UTC calendar date (formatted in server-local time), not the organizer's date
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` gives the override start as a real UTC instant. It is then formatted with `dayjs()`'s default (server-local) zone and compared to `slotStartTime.format(...)` in UTC. For an organizer far from UTC, the override's UTC date can differ from the organizer's date. Example: a UTC+10 override for Nov 12, 08:00-12:00, starts Nov 11 22:00 UTC. Every Nov 11 UTC slot, including the organizer's normal Nov 11 working hours, then counts as 'on the override date but outside it' and is removed. Overridden slots after UTC midnight are also not matched. On a server not running in UTC, the two `format` calls also use different zones. Compare dates in the organizer's time zone (e.g. `slotStartTime.tz(organizerTimeZone)` against the override's local date), or test the interval directly.

findings.title: `===` between two Dayjs objects is always false
findings.body: These are two distinct Dayjs instances, so the zero-length-override branch can never run. If it is meant to treat `start == end` as 'unavailable all day', use `.isSame(...)`. Otherwise, remove it.

contracts.action: checkIfIsAvailable now filters slots by per-user date overrides and working hours before checking busy times
contracts.equivalent_path: getSlots in packages/lib/slots.ts already applies overrides/working hours while generating slots; getWorkingHours produces the working-hours entries
contracts.before_after: Before: only busy times were checked. After: an override match returns true without the busy check (line 133-135), and the working-hours check requires the slot to sit inside every entry for that day
contracts.visible_effect: Booking page shows slots that overlap existing bookings on override days, and hides valid slots for split or UTC-crossing schedules
contracts.failure_mode: No error; slots wrongly shown or hidden without any signal

contracts.action: getSlots shifts override minutes by the invitee/organizer offset difference
contracts.equivalent_path: getUserAvailability builds overrides as organizer wall-clock time stored as UTC
contracts.before_after: Before: raw UTC minutes. After: shifted by inviteeOffset - organizerOffset using override.timeZone, which getSchedule now passes in
contracts.visible_effect: Override slots appear at the right invitee-local times
contracts.failure_mode: If override.timeZone is undefined (it is optional in TimeRange), tz() falls back to the default zone
contracts.open_question: Do overrides that cross invitee midnight after the shift (endTime < startTime) produce correct slots in buildSlots?

summary:
I found two blockers in the new date-override and working-hours checks in `checkIfIsAvailable` (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts`). Both fail silently: no error or log tells anyone that slots were wrongly shown or hidden.

**Blockers**
- **Busy check skipped on override days (line 133):** a slot inside a date override returns `true` before `busy.every(...)` runs. Existing bookings and calendar events on any day with an override no longer block slots, so invitees can double-book the host.
- **Working-hours check too strict (line 139):** a slot is rejected if it falls outside any single working-hours entry for its weekday. `getWorkingHours` in `packages/lib/availability.ts` (lines 76-121) often produces several entries per day: one per range, plus extra entries when local hours cross UTC midnight. Split schedules like 9-12 and 13-17 lose every slot, and so does the part of a schedule that crosses UTC midnight.

**Fixes**
- **Wrong `end` value (line 142):** `end` is computed from the slot's start time, so slots that run past the end of working hours are kept.
- **Multiple overrides on one date (line 106):** a slot inside the second override is rejected because it lies outside the first.
- **Override date compared on the wrong calendar (line 110):** the override's date is matched against the slot's UTC date, formatted in the server's local zone, instead of the organizer's date. For organizers far from UTC, an override can wipe out normal working hours on the next or previous day. I'm less certain of this one because it depends on what zone the server runs in.

**To consider**
- **Dead comparison (line 114):** `===` between two Dayjs objects is always false, so the zero-length-override branch never runs.

The changes in `packages/lib/slots.ts`, `packages/types/schedule.d.ts` and the new test look reasonable. One question stays open: whether overrides that cross the invitee's midnight after the time-zone shift still produce correct slots.
